Case 01 · Medical devices sales team · March 2026

Lisbon, the river and Sintra

In March 2026, a medical devices sales team of 96 guests travelled to Portugal for a four-day programme costing €2,950 per guest. The qualification rule rewarded consultants who exceeded annual territory targets. The schedule paired technical sessions with private tram charters, a long lunch overlooking the Tagus, and an evening dinner on a rooftop terrace above the river. On the final day, private coaches carried the group through Sintra before returning to Lisbon for a farewell reception. The team returned on 22 March 2026 with transfers and return flights coordinated by three on-site tour directors.

Who qualified

Consultants who exceeded their annual territory targets.

Case 02 · Software sales leaders · September 2025

Dolomites, hut to hut

In September 2025, 38 software sales leaders completed a three-night mountain programme priced at €2,180 per guest. Built for senior account executives who reached multi-year expansion quotas, the itinerary replaced traditional conference halls with alpine paths. The group walked high meadow trails between pale limestone peaks, shared family-style dinners in high-altitude mountain huts, and conducted strategy reviews in quiet lodge libraries. Transfers from the regional airport and all luggage movements were managed directly by our team. The group completed their journey on 21 September 2025 supported by our round-the-clock duty line.

Who qualified

Senior account executives who reached multi-year expansion quotas.

Case 03 · Insurance top sellers · February 2025

Cape Town and the winelands

In February 2025, 120 insurance top sellers gathered for a five-night long-haul programme across the Western Cape at €4,100 per guest. The programme balanced vineyard tastings and coastal excursions with a private catamaran cruise in the shadow of Table Mountain. With four tour directors deployed across the group, transfers between Cape Town and the winelands operated without delay. Two communal dinners brought the entire commercial division together before the departure flight on 16 February 2025. A thorough debrief session with the client leadership team followed ten working days after arrival.

The top sellers of the insurance division.

Case 04 · Logistics sales team · January 2026

Copenhagen harbour kick-off

In January 2026, a logistics sales team of 64 guests held a three-night winter summit in Denmark priced at €1,620 per guest. The objective was aligning regional leaders following a corporate reorganization. Activities included morning bicycle rides along quiet harbour quays, private architectural boat tours, and curated dinners in renovated waterfront warehouses. Two dedicated tour directors oversaw hotel check-ins, meeting rooms, and scheduled group transfers. The programme concluded smoothly on 25 January 2026, delivering measurable team cohesion ahead of the new operational calendar.

pages.title: How we plan
pages.content:
Five stages.

Our planning methodology guides corporate travel from the initial budget allocation through to the return flight debrief.

Budget → return flight

Lead time

Budget to return flight

Ideal
6–12 months

Minimum
10 weeks

Debrief
+10 days

The five planning stages

We manage every contract, timeline, and transport detail so your leadership team can focus entirely on your people.

Our structured process advances across five defined milestones.

01

Budget and rule

Week 1

We establish your overall budget, guest headcount and the qualifying rule, to anchor every later decision.

What we need from you. Your budget range, the headcount and the reward rule, in writing.

02

Three destinations, costed

Weeks 2–3

We present three researched, itemised destinations that match your travel window and flight preferences.

What we need from you. A travel window, and any places you would rule out.

03

Site visit and final programme

Weeks 4–8

We inspect hotels and venues on site, lock the dinners and finalise the minute-by-minute programme.

What we need from you. A named contact for the site visit and the dates you can travel.

Stage 03: the planner and the venue manager walk the ballroom before the programme is final.

04

Announce to the team and register guests

From 6 months out

You launch the reward internally while we manage registrations, room allocations and flight manifests.

What we need from you. Your announcement date, and the guest list as it firms up.

05

Travel, return flight and debrief

On the trip + 10 working days

Our tour directors run every transfer, backed by the duty line, followed by a full debrief within ten working days.

What we need from you. A leader on the trip, and a debrief slot in the diary.

Stage 05: the group lands; the debrief is booked within ten working days.

A typical day on programme

During travel, our tour directors execute a consistent daily rhythm that balances punctuality with personal comfort.

07:30

Your tour director is at the breakfast desk with the printed day sheet.

09:00

Coaches leave for the morning excursion or the meeting venue.

13:00

A seated group lunch.

16:00

Unhurried free time to rest or explore.

19:30

The group dinner.

23:00

The lead tour director’s last check-in with the 24 h duty line.

How far in advance should a programme be planned?

We recommend an ideal planning horizon of six to twelve months prior to departure. This lead time secures optimal flight allocations, preferred hotel bedroom blocks, and private dining spaces for groups of 20 to 120 guests. However, our operational framework accommodates a strict minimum lead time of ten weeks for urgent corporate retreats or kick-off summits. When working within condensed timelines, early alignment on qualification criteria and swift approval of our three costed destination options ensure seamless execution before departure.

Ideal lead time

6 to 12 months before departure: the best flight allocations, hotel room blocks and private dining rooms.

Minimum lead time

10 weeks, for urgent retreats and kick-off summits.

First costed proposal

Within weeks 2–3 of your brief, with three destinations.

Announcement to your team

From six months out, once the destination is chosen.

How are destination proposals selected?

Since 2012, our team has delivered travel programmes across 23 tested locations.

We evaluate every prospective destination against three strict operational criteria. First, travel links must be direct and dependable, keeping flight or rail times under four hours for short-haul journeys from major hubs. Second, partner hotels must provide certified four-star quality, verified bedroom blocks, and private dining rooms capable of seating up to 120 guests together. Third, all regional transfer operators, mountain guides, and catering partners must pass direct on-site vetting by our senior planners before a route is proposed to clients.

Southern European and coastal destinations

Our southern European portfolio features Lisbon, Seville, and the dramatic southern coast of Iceland. In Lisbon and Sintra, groups of up to 96 guests enjoy rooftop riverside dining and historic tram routes over three nights. Our Seville and Andalusian coast programme hosts up to 72 guests across three nights, featuring quiet palace courtyards, orange groves, and regional culinary traditions. In southern Iceland, teams of up to 54 guests complete a four-night itinerary across black-sand shores, glacier valleys, and coastal hot springs with dedicated private coach transfers.

Alpine, northern and long-haul routes

For alpine, northern, or intercontinental briefs, we operate proven itineraries in the Dolomites, Copenhagen, and Cape Town. Our Dolomites retreat welcomes groups of up to 38 guests for three nights of hut-to-hut hiking and quiet mountain strategy sessions. In Denmark, the Copenhagen harbour kick-off accommodates up to 64 guests for three nights of cycling, architecture, and waterfront dining. In South Africa, our five-night Cape Town and winelands programme hosts up to 120 guests, combining coastal catamaran sailing with private estate tastings.

pages.content:

Origins and the meaning of Hobi

Based at Harbour House in Port Arden, our independent agency plans and delivers travel programmes for teams across Europe.

Hobi Journeys was founded in 2012 by Maren Holt and Daniel Okoro after organizing the annual sales trip for their former employer. They recognized that corporate reward travel was often treated as an afterthought, lacking personal operational care. The word hobi represents our guiding belief: transforming the everyday work of business into an exceptional day out. Operating from Harbour House, 9 Wharf Lane in Port Arden, our planners coordinate travel logistics, hotel partnerships, and private itineraries that celebrate company milestones with calm precision.

Key milestones from 2012 to 2026

Our growth has followed a deliberate and steady progression over fourteen years.

2012

First programme: 38 guests to Lisbon.

2016

Our own tour-director team is formed.

2019

First long-haul programme: five nights in Cape Town.

2023

The sales-retreat line for smaller leadership groups.

2026

The 41st programme, and 3,860 guests across 23 destinations.

Why do we deploy dedicated tour directors?

We believe seamless group travel requires experienced human leadership on the ground rather than digital self-service tools. We provide one professional tour director for every 30 guests on every programme we operate. Our tour directors manage morning check-ins at 07:30, coordinate coach departures at 09:00, supervise hotel transfers, and oversee group dining arrangements. Supported by our 24-hour operational duty line, our directors resolve travel irregularities quietly in the background so client leaders can engage fully with their top-performing colleagues.

Meet the seven people →

Who accompanies the team during travel?

Every journey is personally accompanied by our dedicated tour directors, led by Sofie Lindqvist and Kwame Asante. We maintain a firm staffing ratio of one director per 30 guests for groups ranging from 20 to 120 participants. Our tour directors travel on the same flights or rail connections, supervise private transfers, manage hospitality desks each morning, and remain on site through evening dinners. This hands-on presence ensures immediate assistance for every guest while maintaining direct contact with our 24-hour duty line.

pages.title: Brief us
pages.content:
Brief us.

Tell us about your team size, preferred travel window, and incentive targets. We will evaluate your parameters and prepare three costed destination proposals tailored to your budget.

Information needed for your brief

To begin planning your corporate programme, we require four basic parameters about your team. First, confirm your expected group size between 20 and 120 guests. Second, indicate your preferred departure window, ideally six to twelve months in advance or ten weeks at minimum. Third, identify your budget tier, starting from €980 per guest for retreats up to €3,900 for long-haul journeys. Finally, outline your internal reward rule so our planners can tailor travel milestones directly to your qualification standards.

What are the standard budget tiers?

We structure our proposals across four realistic commercial tiers to match diverse corporate goals. Options include under €1,500 per guest for focused regional kick-offs, 1,500 to €2,500 per guest for standard European short-haul trips, 2,500 to €4,000 per guest for premium experiences such as Lisbon or the Dolomites, and above €4,000 per guest for comprehensive long-haul itineraries like Cape Town. Every tier includes transport, four-star accommodation, transfers, tour directors, and our round-the-clock duty line.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
Contact.

Reach our planning office in Port Arden for new programme briefs, active travel questions, or supplier partnerships. Our team is available by telephone and email Monday through Friday.

Getting to Harbour House

Our office is conveniently located along the Port Arden waterfront. Visitors arriving by train can walk from Port Arden Central station in approximately six minutes via the pedestrian quayside. Please note that Harbour House does not offer on-site visitor car parking; visitors arriving by vehicle should use public parking facilities in the town centre. For those commuting by bicycle, secure visitor cycle racks are available inside our private entrance courtyard adjacent to the main building entrance.

How does the 24-hour duty line operate?

While standard office hours run Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 18:00, our operations room maintains a continuous 24-hour duty line whenever a client group is travelling. This private communication line connects directly to our on-duty operational managers and lead tour directors in the field. Whether managing an unexpected flight delay, rescheduling private coach transfers, or coordinating emergency medical care, our round-the-clock duty desk provides immediate operational resolution until all travellers return home safely.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Privacy.

This policy outlines how Hobi Journeys collects, processes, and protects personal data during the planning and delivery of corporate travel programmes. We handle all guest information with strict confidentiality and care.

Information we collect for travel programmes

Hobi Journeys, operating from Harbour House, 9 Wharf Lane, Port Arden, collects only personal data required to plan and execute corporate travel. When a client submits a brief, we collect corporate contact details, team sizes between 20 and 120 guests, and travel preferences. During guest registration, we collect legal names, passport details, dietary requirements, and flight manifests necessary for airline ticketing and four-star hotel reservations. We do not sell, rent, or trade participant data to external marketing agencies.

Data retention and communication choices

We retain travel records only as long as necessary to complete your programme and satisfy legal accounting requirements. Detailed guest manifests and rooming lists are archived following the completion of our formal client debrief within ten working days of the return flight. Contact details for our monthly letter, The Itinerary, are held separately and used solely to send dispatches on the first Tuesday of the month. Subscribers can opt out at any time using the unsubscribe link provided.

How can you access or update your information?

Clients and travelling guests have the right to request access to the personal data we hold, correct inaccurate details, or request data deletion where statutory obligations permit. Inquiries regarding data protection, access requests, or communications preferences should be directed to our data coordinator by email at hello@hobi-journeys.example or by telephone at +44 1632 960 418. Our office operates Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 18:00, and our team responds to all formal data inquiries within two working days.

posts.title: Why we still hand out boarding passes
posts.excerpt: In an era of mobile booking codes and digital self-service, handing a physical document to a travelling colleague marks the exact moment a corporate sales year becomes a shared reality.
posts.content:
At our welcome desks in hotel lobbies from Lisbon to Copenhagen, you will not find digital touchscreens or self-service check-in kiosks. Instead, you will see a neatly arranged wooden table with crisp printed day sheets, lanyards, and individual boarding passes laid out in alphabetical order. A tour director in a dark blazer stands behind the desk, greeting each guest by name and handing over their travel documents one by one. In a commercial landscape dominated by mobile apps and booking reference codes, this deliberate ritual might appear old-fashioned. To us, it remains one of the most important operational moments of the entire programme.

When Maren Holt and Daniel Okoro founded Hobi Journeys in 2012 at Harbour House in Port Arden, they established a founding philosophy: turning the demanding effort of the everyday sales year into an exceptional day out. Corporate incentive travel is not standard business travel. For twelve months, a commercial team of 20 to 120 people has tracked targets, navigated complex pipelines, and carried the weight of performance metrics. When top performers arrive at an airport gate or hotel lobby, the psychological transition from high-pressure corporate office to shared retreat must be immediate and tangible.

A digital ticket on a smartphone screen keeps the traveller tethered to their everyday work environment. The moment a guest opens their phone to retrieve a digital bar code, they inevitably encounter unread client emails, pending chat notifications, and missed messages from the office. A physical boarding pass interrupts that administrative routine. It is an unequivocal physical signal that the travel logistics are entirely handled by someone else. When a tour director hands a colleague their pass, the unspoken message is clear: your work is done for the year, and our team has assumed responsibility for the journey.

This hands-on attention extends directly into the daily operational schedule of every programme we run. We provide one dedicated tour director for every 30 guests, ensuring that our people are present at every critical juncture. At 07:30 each morning, our tour director is stationed at the breakfast desk with the daily schedule sheet, confirming transfer times and dietary arrangements. At 09:00, private coaches depart promptly with every seat verified and luggage accounted for. Whether coordinating an afternoon catamaran in Cape Town, a quiet alpine walk in the Dolomites, or a historic tram charter in Lisbon, our directors ensure that no guest ever has to troubleshoot a transport reservation or confirm a dining room table.

Across 41 delivered programmes and 3,860 travellers, we have learned that the success of a sales retreat is measured by how thoroughly participants can disengage from logistical worry. Behind every seamless four-day trip lies rigorous back-office coordination: a 24-hour duty line tracking flight statuses, meticulous venue inspections, and round-the-clock crisis readiness. Handing over a physical boarding pass is simply the outward manifestation of that deep operational care. It establishes trust from the first minute and reminds every participant that their commercial achievements have earned genuine, personal recognition.

posts.title: Writing a reward rule your team believes
posts.excerpt: How clear qualification criteria and honest milestone tracking keep a sales team motivated across four quarters.
posts.content:
A reward trip is only as motivating as the rule that earns it. Teams read the rule in the first week of the year and test it against what they know about their own pipeline. If it feels arbitrary, they stop believing in the trip.

The rules that work are short, measurable and visible. One number, one date and a place where everyone can see where they stand at the end of each quarter. We ask clients to write the rule before we cost the first destination.

Where a rule has changed mid-year the trip has usually suffered. If the target must move, say so early, say why and keep the destination fixed. The team is travelling towards a place, not a spreadsheet.

posts.title: The day after the return flight
posts.excerpt: Closing the loop with itemised budget reconciliation, supplier settlement and a team debrief within ten working days.
posts.content:
The programme is not finished when the group lands. The day after the return flight our planner reopens the budget and compares it, line by line, with what was spent on the trip.

Within ten working days the client receives an itemised reconciliation, a list of supplier settlements and a short debrief from the tour directors: what worked, what to change and what the guests said at the last dinner.

The debrief is the first page of the next brief. Most of our repeat programmes begin with it.
